JUDGMENT Husband and daughter of Anjali Devi M.C. @ Anjali filed petition under Section 166 of IMV Act claiming compensation worth of Rs.1,50,00,000/- from the respondents, who are the owner and insurer of the Honda Activa bearing No.KA-44-W-9459 alleging that on 06.03.2023 at 11.00 a.m.,
when Anjali Devi travelling by sitting on the pillion of Honda Activa bearing No.KA-44-W- 9459 rode by respondent No.1 - Soumya on Pavagada - Kalyanadurga road, near Anjaneyaswamy temple,
Palavalli Katte, Pavagada taluk, respondent No.1 - Soumya negligently rode Honda Activa dashed the same to a dog, which came across the road, fell along with Scooter and Anjali Devi, thereby caused the accident, caused grievous injuries to Anjali Devi.
2.

Immediately after the accident Anjali Devi has been shifted to Government hospital, Pavagada wherein first aid has been provided, then shifted to Siddaganga Hospital, Tumkur, then shifted to Sparsh Hospital, Bengaluru wherein on 09.03.2023 Anjali Devi succumbed to those injuries.

3. As on the date of accident deceased Anjali Devi being aged about 46 years, used to earn Rs.75,000/- per month by working as Govt. High School Teacher, B.K.Halli, Pavagada Taluk,
Tumkur District.

4. Regarding accident Pavagada police registered a case in Crime No.55/2023.
5.
In response to the notice, respondent No.1 appeared through her Advocate, but neither filed written statement nor participated in the proceedings.

6. In response to the notice respondent No.2 - Insurance company appeared through his Advocate,
filed written statement denying the allegation regarding reason and mode of accident, age,
occupation and income of deceased Anjali Devi.

7. On the basis of the pleadings on 31.12.2024, this Authority has framed the following issues:

sentences.text:
Whether the petitioners prove that on 06.03.2023 at about 11.00 a.m., on Pavagada -
Kalyandurga road, near Anjineyaswamy temple, Palavalli Katte, Pavagada taluk, Tumkur district, in view of the negligent use of the Honda Activa bearing Reg. No.KA-44-W-9459 by respondent No.1 - Smt.Soumya, Honda Activa dashed to a dog therefore Honda Activa fell along with Sowmya - rider,
Anjali Devi M.C., pillion rider, resulting in the grievous injuries to Anjali Devi who succumbed to those injuries on 09.03.2023 at Sparsha hospital, Bengaluru?
2. Whether the petitioners are entitled to compensation? If so, how much and from whom?
3. What order?
8. On 18.09.2024, 25.10.2024, 19.02.2025 petitioner No.1 deposed as P.W.1 and produced 19 documents at Ex.P.1 to P.19.

On 25.11.2024, 19.02.2025 petitioners produced evidence of Medical Record Officer at Sparsha hospital and Head Master, Govt. High School, Bettada Kelagina halli,
Pavagada taluk as P.W.2 and P.W.3 and produced 7 documents at Ex.P.20 to Ex.P.27.
9.

entities.text: Govt. High School, Bettada Kelagina halli
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: I heard the arguments submitted on behalf of both the contesting parties and perused the records.

10. On the basis of material on record, my findings on the above issues are as under:
Issue No.1 ... In the Affirmative; Issue No.2 ...
Petitioners are entitle to receive Rs.71,14,992/- with current and future interest at 6%p.a. from the respondents as compensation.
Issue No.3 ...

As per final order for the following:-
REASONS 11. Issue No.1:- In the evidence P.W.1-Nanjundappa stated that on 06.03.2023 at 11.00 a.m., when Anjali Devi was traveling by sitting on the pillion of Honda Activa bearing No.KA-44-W-9459 rode by Soumya on the left side of Pavagada - Kalyanadurga road, near Anjaneyaswamy temple, Palavalli Katte, Pavagada taluk, Soumya dashed the Honda Activa to a dog, lost control, fell along with Scooter and pillion rider Anjali Devi, thereby caused the accident, caused grievous injuries to Anjali Devi.

12. P.W.1 stated that, immediately after the accident Anjali Devi has been shifted to Government hospital, Pavagada wherein first aid has been provided, then shifted to Siddaganga Hospital,
Tumkur, then admitted to Sparsh Hospital, Bengaluru wherein on 09.03.2023 Anjali Devi succumbed to the injuries.
13.
In the written statement respondent No.2 denied the allegation regarding reason and mode of accident.

Nanjudappa vs Soumya H M on 8 April, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/192348531/
3 14.

sentences.text: In the cross-examination, P.W.1 stated that on 06.03.2023 his wife met with an accident, after 3 or 4 days of accident, his son-in-law Lokesh filed complaint.
P.W.1 submitted that he never witnessed the accident.
15. In the evidence P.W.2 - MRO of Sparsh Hospital produced MLC Register extract and copy of police intimation at Ex.P.21
and P.22.
16. In the evidence P.W.3 stated nothing regarding reason and mode of accident.

17. Ex.P.1 is the copy of the FIR with complaint pertaining to Crime No.55/2023 registered by Pavagada police against respondent No.1 - Soumya, rider of Honda Activa bearing No.KA-44-W-9459 for having committed offence punishable under Section 279 and 337 of IPC regarding accident taken place on 06.03.2023 at 11.00 a.m. resulting in the injuries to Anjali Devi on the basis of complaint presented by Lokesh, S/o.Nagaraja.
Ex.P.2 is the copy of information dated 09.03.2023 forwarded by Investigating Officer to Prl.Civil Judge and JMFC, Pavagada in Cr.No.55/2023 about the death of Anjali Dev I.
Ex.P.3 is the copy of spot mahazar with sketch of the place of accident.
Ex.P.4 is the copy of Scooty seizure mahazar.
Ex.P.5 is the copy of Inquest Mahazar with the statements of relatives/witnesses.
Ex . P.6
is the copy of P.M.Report.
Ex . P.8
is the copy of Motor Vehicle Accident Report.

18. Ex.P.9 is the copy of charge sheet filed by Pavagada police in crime No.55/2023 against respondent No.1 - Soumya, rider of Honda Activa bearing No.KA-44-W- 9459 for having committed offence punishable under Section 279, 304(A) of IPC.
In Ex.P.21 - MLC Register extract, appearance of Anjali Devi with injuries alleged to have been suffered on 06.03.2023 at 10.30 a.m., near Pavagada Highway as pillion rider is mentioned.
Ex.P.22 is the copy of police intimation dated 6.03.2023 forwarded by CMO, Sparsch Hospital to PSI, Yashavanthapura P.S., Bengaluru.
19. In this case, respondents have not produced any type of evidence to disbelieve the evidence placed by the petitioners regarding reason, mode and consequence of accident.

20. Hence, I have concluded that on 06.03.2023 at 11.00 a.m. when Anjali Devi was travelling by sitting on the pillion of Honda Activa bearing No.KA-44-W-9459 rode by respondent No.1 - Soumya on Pavagada - Kalyanadurga road, near Anjaneyaswamy temple, Palavalli Katte, Pavagada taluk,
respondent No.1 negligently rode the Scooter dashed the same to a dog, fell along with Anjali Devi,
thereby caused the accident, caused injuries, Anjali Devi who succumbed to those injuries on 09.03.2023 at Sparsh Hospital, Bengaluru.
Hence, I answer Issue No.1 in the Affirmative.
21. Issue No.2:

In the evidence P.W.1 stated that as on the date of accident, Anjali Devi being aged about 46 years, used to earn Rs.75,000/- per month by working as a Teacher in Government High school and used to contribute entire income to the family.
22. In the written statement respondent No.2 denied the allegation regarding age, occupation and income of the deceased Anjali Devi.

sentences.text: In the cross-examination, P.W.1 denied the suggestion that as on the date of alleged incident, his wife never earning Rs.75,000/- p.m.
P.W.1 admitted that as per salary slip during February 2023 his wife might have received Rs.55,520/- as gross salary.
P.W.1 stated that date of birth of his wife Anjali Devi is 07.07.1977.

P.W.1 admitted that in P.M.Report missing of the several organs (heart,
liver, both kidneys are mentioned).
During cross examination of P.W.1, learned advocate for petitioner submitted that due to missing of organs or donation of organs, hospital given reduction worth of Rs.2,00,000/- in the medical bills.

24. In the evidence P.W.2-MRO of Sparsh Hospital produced 2 Case files at Ex.P.23 & 24.
25.

In the evidence P.W.3 - Head Master, Government Hish School, B.K.Halli, Pavagada taluk produced copy of Service Register, Pay slips of Anjali Devi from September 2022 to February 2023,
copy of the attendance register at Ex.P.25 to 27.
26.
P.W.3 submitted that as per Service Register as on 30.03.2023, 101 earned leave are in credit in the leave account of Anjali Devi.

P.W.3 admitted as per salary slip during February 2023, gross salary of Anjali Devi was Rs.55,522/-.
27.
In Ex.P.10 - copy of the Aadhar card and Ex.P.13 - ID card issued by the Education Department, date of birth of Anjali Devi is noted as 03.07.1977 (46 years as on the date of incident).

Salary slip marked at Ex.P.26 shows that during February, 2023 Anjali Devi received Rs.39,800/- as basic salary, Rs.12,338/- as D.A., Rs.3,184/- as HRA, Rs.200/-
as medical allowance, gross salary is Rs.55,522/-, in which Rs.200, Rs.240/-, Rs.1672/-, Rs.5,000/-
and Rs.4,000/- are deducted towards professional tax, EGIS, LIC, GPF and KGID respectively.
28.

In this case there are no reasons to disbelieve the evidence placed by P.W.1 regarding age,
occupation and income of deceased as on the date of incident.
Aadhar cards shows that petitioners are the husband and daughter of the deceased Anjali Devi.

29. Hence, I have inferred that, it is fit and proper to assess the compensation under the head of loss of dependency presuming that as on the date of incident Anjali Devi being aged about 46 years, used to earn Rs.51,938/- p.m. as salary (basic + DA - professional tax), by working as Teacher, by adding 25% as future prospects and by deducting 1/3rd of her income towards personal expenses and by applying multiplier '13', in the following terms:
Age of the deceased Anjali Devi as on - 46 years the date of accident - Monthly permanent income excluding - Rs.51,938/- professional tax as on the date of incident

Add: 25% towards future prospects - Rs.64,922/- (51,938/- + 12,984/- =
64,922/-) Less: 1/3rd towards personal expenses - Rs.43,282/- of the deceased Anjali Devi (64,922/- - 21,640/- = 43,282/-)

Annual income of the deceased - Rs.5,19,384/-
 43,282/- x12  Multiplier Applicable - 13 Nanjudappa vs Soumya H M on 8 April, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/192348531/
5  Loss of dependency =5,19,384 x 13 - Rs.67,51,992/-
30.

sentences.text:
Hence, I award Rs.67,51,992/- towards loss of dependency, Rs.16,500/- towards loss of estate, Rs.16,500/- towards funeral expenses and Rs.88,000/-
towards loss of consortium to petitioners No.1 and 2 at the rate of Rs.44,000/- each.

Medical bills shows that since from the time of accident til 09.03.2022 petitioners get treated Anjali Devi by spending Rs.2,20,000/- excluding reduction given by hospital due to donation of the organs.

Hence,
I award Rs.2,20,000/- towards treatment charges and Rs.20,000/- towards attendants and conveyance charges.

Sl. Head of Compensation Amount/Rs  No.
 1. Loss of dependency 67,51,992-00  2. Loss of estate 16,500-00
3 . Funeral expenses 16,500-00
4. Loss of Consortium to 88,000-00  petitioners No.1 & 2 at  Rs.44,000/each  5.
Treatment charges 2,22,000.00  6.
Attendant charges, conveyance 20,000.00  and nourishment charges

Hence, I came to the conclusion that the petitioners being husband and daughter of deceased Anjali Devi are entitle to receive Rs.71,14,992/- with current and future interest at the rate of 6% p.a.
as compensation from the respondents.
32. In the written statement respondent No.2 - Insurance company admitted the subsistence of the policy with respect Honda Activa bearing No.KA-44-W-9459 as on the date of incident.
In the reply submitted to the notice under Section 133 of IMV Act dated 02.05.2023, respondent No.1 - Soumya noted her Driving Licence number.
Hence, it is clear that as on the date of incident, respondent No.1 has not violated any terms of the policy.

Hence, I came to the conclusion that the respondents being the owner and insurer of Honda Activa bearing No.KA-44- W-9459 are liable to pay compensation and an award is to be passed directing the respondents No.1 and 2 to pay compensation to the petitioners,

Hence, I answer issue No.2 accordingly and pass the following:

sentences.text: The petition filed under Section 166 of IMV Act is hereby partly allowed.

The respondents No.1 and 2 being the owner and insurer of Honda Activa bearing No.KA-44-W-9459 shall either jointly or severally pay Rs.71,14,992/- (Rupees Seventy one lakhs Fourteen thousand nine hundred and ninety two only) with current and future interest at the rate of 6% p.a., to petitioners towards compensation.
The respondent No.2, being the Insurer of the Honda Activa bearing No.KA-44-W-9459 shall deposit the compensation amount with interest within 3 months from today.
The compensation amount and interest are distributed among petitioners at the ratio of 20:80.
After deposit of the compensation amount, entire compensation amount with interest may be released to the petitioner No.1 by crediting the same to his bank account directly.

After deposit of the compensation amount, 25% of compensation amount and interest allotted in favour of petitioner No.2, who is now attained the age of majority,
may be released by crediting the same to her bank account directly.
Surplus compensation amount with interest shall be deposited in any of the bank in the name of petitioner No.2 for a period of two years without permitting to create any encumbrances.
Advocate's fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/-.
Draw an Award accordingly.

(Dictated to the Stenographer Gr.I, transcribed by her, corrected, signed and then pronounced by me in the Open Court on this the 8th day of April, 2025)
(J.N.SUBRAMANYA) Chief Judge, Court of Small Causes & Member, Prl. M.A.C.T.
Bangalore.
